enonce_markdown: Which HTML tag defines the largest heading on a web page?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

HTML has six heading levels, `<h1>` to `<h6>`: the lower the number, the larger the heading.

### Solution

`<h1>` gives the largest heading and `<h6>` the smallest. `<head>` is not a heading tag: it holds information about the page, and `<title>` sets the text shown on the browser tab.

**Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown: Which piece of code displays the word Results as a link to the page `results.html`?
corrige_markdown: ### Method reminder A hyperlink uses the anchor tag `` with the attribute `href` giving the destination; the text between the opening and closing tags is what the visitor clicks. ### Solution `Results` is correct: the destination is in `href` and the clickable text is between the tags. `src` is used for images, not links; `` belongs to the head of the page; and the last option puts the destination as the visible text, not as the target. **Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown: Which of the following HTML fragments has its tags correctly nested?
corrige_markdown: ### Method reminder Tags must be closed in the reverse order in which they were opened: the last tag opened is the first one closed. ### Solution `Hello` opens b then i, and closes i then b: correct. `Hello` and `Hello` close the tags in the wrong order, and `Hello` never closes ``. **Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: Write the HTML code of a web page that has the title "My School" on the browser tab, a level-1 heading "Welcome", a paragraph "Government Bilingual High School", a horizontal line, and a bulleted list with two items: Science and Arts. (6 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder An HTML page has a `` (with the ``) and a `<body>` (the visible content). A bulleted list uses `<ul>` with one `<li>` per item. ### Solution ```html <html> <head> <title>My School

Welcome

Government Bilingual High School

  • Science
  • Arts
``` - `` is inside `<head>`: it appears on the tab, not on the page. - `<h1>` gives the heading and `<p>` the paragraph. - `<hr>` draws the horizontal line. - `<ul>` with two `<li>` items gives the bulleted list. - Every tag opened is closed in the right order (checked by a parser script). Marking idea: html/head/body structure (2), title (1), heading and paragraph (1), hr (1), list (1).

enonce_markdown:
A browser opens this page: ```html

Market list

  1. Tomatoes
  2. Onions
  3. Fish
  • Salt
  • Oil
``` Which description of the displayed page is correct?

choix.texte: A heading, three numbered items, a line, then two bulleted items
A heading, then five numbered items
A heading, three bulleted items, a line, then two numbered items
A heading, a line, then five bulleted items

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

`<ol>` numbers its `<li>` items (1, 2, 3...) while `<ul>` marks them with bullets; `<hr>` draws a line between two blocks.

### Solution

The page shows the heading "Market list", then a numbered list with three items (1 Tomatoes, 2 Onions, 3 Fish; counted by a parser script), then a horizontal line, then a bulleted list with two items (Salt, Oil). The numbering of the first list does not continue in the second list because the second one is not an ordered list.

**Answer: A.**
